U1: Add option to support Apache Ambari installed Spring XD on YARN - establish cluster easily.
U2: Use spring-cloud-config server for spring-bus modules - centrally manage external properties.
U3: Investigate channel performance issues in Spring Integration 4.2 - determine bottlenecks, take corrective actions.
U4: Measure baseline serialization characteristics in XD - determine areas of performance improvement.
U5: Review current spring-bus architecture and design specs - address foundation level gaps.
U6: Upgrade Spring XD from 1.2 RC to 1.2 GA using the Ambari plugin, with documentation.
U7: Support fsUri = file:// to use Hadoop LocalFileSystem instead of running cluster (for jdbchdfs job).
U8: Option to specify system properties passed to Sqoop job running in own Java process (memory usage, connector options).

These look like actual historical Spring XD JIRA stories (XD-1.2 era, circa 2015).

technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Implement Apache Ambari support as a custom Ambari stack/service definition with Python-based service scripts (install, start, stop, status) that provision Spring XD admin and container nodes on YARN, reusing the existing Spring XD YARN deployment support (Spring for Apache Hadoop / Spring YARN) rather than building a new deployment mechanism.
U1: Manage XD-on-YARN configuration (yarn-site, servers.yml, Hadoop client config) through Ambari configuration templates so cluster settings are centrally editable from the Ambari UI.

U2: Integrate spring-cloud-config by adding Spring Cloud Config client bootstrap to the spring-bus modules, externalizing bus and module properties into a Git-backed config repository and defining explicit property precedence (config server over local files).

U3: Use JMH-based microbenchmarks plus JVM profiling (JFR/YourKit-style) to isolate Spring Integration 4.2 channel bottlenecks; corrective actions are limited to code/configuration fixes within XD, with any upstream SI defects reported rather than fixed.

U4: Build a repeatable serialization benchmark harness covering the XD-supported codecs/serializers (Java serialization, Kryo, JSON) across representative payload sizes and module types to establish the baseline.

U5: Perform the spring-bus architecture review against the existing design specs, then implement only foundation-level gap fixes (small refactorings and contract corrections), avoiding a bus redesign.
U6: Implement the 1.2 RC to 1.2 GA upgrade through the Ambari plugin's package replacement and configuration schema migration mechanism, preserving existing user configuration.

U7: Support fsUri=file:// by relaxing HDFS-specific validation in the HDFS-aware modules/jobs (e.g., jdbchdfs) so the Hadoop LocalFileSystem is selected when the file scheme is used; multi-container local-file splitting is documented as a known caveat, not engineered around.
U8: Add a new module option (e.g., a system-properties/java-options property) on the Sqoop job module whose value is appended to the command line of the separately spawned Sqoop JVM process.
assumptions: A single experienced developer (familiar with Spring XD, Spring Integration, Spring Cloud Config, Ambari, and the Hadoop ecosystem) performs all work; estimates are net effort, not elapsed time.
The Spring XD 1.2 RC codebase, build system, and CI infrastructure already exist; estimates cover only this increment's user stories, not base product development.

The introductory Spring Framework background in the specification (including the Java 17+ note for Spring Framework 6.0) is contextual only; the work targets the Spring XD 1.2 line and its supported JDK.
Multi-node YARN/Hadoop test clusters and Ambari test environments are available for installation and upgrade testing; environment procurement is excluded.
U6 builds on the Ambari plugin delivered in U1 (dependency within the same increment), so upgrade effort only covers the RC-to-GA delta.
Investigation stories U3, U4, and U5 include producing written findings and limited corrective actions/gap fixes; large-scale redesigns or upstream framework fixes are out of scope.
U7 correctness is required for single-node/local setups; distributed local-file behavior across containers on multiple machines is only documented as a caveat.
User-facing documentation effort is included only where explicitly requested (U6) plus brief usage notes for U7/U8; no full documentation overhaul is assumed.
Code review rework and integration testing are estimated as separate cross-cutting activities applied to the whole increment.
